answer: Randomized admission lottery: each period a public comet-style beacon commits a seed before applicants arrive, then assigns identities to a small fixed cohort using a cipher the attacker cannot invert without the seed. An attacker flooding thousands of cheap identities gains almost nothing, since each has only a slim chance of admission within that horizon and must pay registration and monitoring costs on every attempt. Expected cost per successful entry rises roughly linearly with the number of fakes submitted.
